name: Gadolinium
occurrence: Found in gadolinite and monazite ores; named after the mineral gadolinite, itself named for chemist Johan Gadolin.
majorUses: MRI contrast agent (gadolinium compounds enhance image clarity)
Neutron shielding in nuclear reactors (extremely high neutron absorption)
notableCharacteristics: One of only a handful of elements that are ferromagnetic near room temperature, alongside iron, cobalt, and nickel — though gadolinium loses this property just above normal room temperature.
whyHere: Its half-filled 4f⁷ plus one 5d electron gives an unusually strong, well-aligned magnetic moment, which is exactly why gadolinium is both ferromagnetic near room temperature and effective at altering the magnetic signal MRI machines detect.
didYouKnow: Millions of MRI scans every year use an injected gadolinium-based contrast agent to make blood vessels and tumours show up more clearly — one of the very few lanthanides most people have actually had inside their body.
genZNote: You've probably had this injected into you during an MRI and didn't even know it was a lanthanide. Wild.
